title: Terrorism Trends Data Visualiser
tagline: Data Visualisation Website of terrorism statistics around the world
overview: Discover insights and trends within terrorism in countries around the world
problem: Terrorism trends such as modes of attack, weapons used etc. are unclear.
solution: Built a responsive website to aggregate data, identify trends pertaining to terrorism to anticipate modes of attacks and assess countermeasures.
architecture: Database: MongoDB and MySQL hosted on Aiven
metrics: Heatmaps of frequent terrorist attacks, zooming in to attacks and fatalities by year
Transaction and Rollback features to maintain data integrity through ACID principles
Ability for user to add data on new terrorist attacks directly into website
Filters and drilldown tables to uncover patterns and insights
keyContributions: Chart plotting within the website based on terrorism data
Performance Analysis between SQL and NoSQL
learningPoints: SQL outperformed NoSQL in speed by 26 times. This is expected as the strength of SQL is its query speed and NoSQL is its horizontal scaling and schema flexibility
How to plot charts in react native
Learnt how to set up MongoDB and NoSQL databases and perform CRUD on them

challenges.title: React Native was difficult
challenges.description: Being new to the react native framework, it was a challenge to get it to work

challenges.title: Architecture decisions between SQL and NoSQL
challenges.description: Planning for future scalability on whether data can be funnelled into SQL or NoSQL, how to integrate the both of them in one application

challenges.title: Deciding what database tool to use
challenges.description: In hindsight, it might have been better to use PostgreSQL rather than integrating MongoDB and MySQL as our data was still rather structured
